selector.rationale: Soap-bubble appearance and cortical destruction on CT, along with avid enhancement on MRI, are characteristic of Giant Cell Tumor

rejected.label: Osteoma
rejected.why: Osteoma is typically a well-defined, compact bone lesion, which does not match the lytic and destructive nature of the described lesion

rejected.label: Eosinophilic Granuloma
rejected.why: Eosinophilic Granuloma often presents with a single, well-defined lytic lesion, but the described lesion's size, soap-bubble appearance, and soft-tissue component are not typical

rejected.label: Ewing's Sarcoma
rejected.why: Ewing's Sarcoma is a highly aggressive tumor, usually presenting with significant soft-tissue mass and systemic symptoms, which are not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Brown Tumor
rejected.why: Although Brown Tumor can have a soap-bubble appearance, the lack of specific laboratory findings (e.g., hyperparathyroidism) and the lesion's characteristics make Giant Cell Tumor a more likely diagnosis
